catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Analysis based on the runtime input context (pyproject.toml, directory tree, and key file/symbol index) for the Continuous Architecture System (CAS) runner. The repository is an agent-orchestration/governance toolkit: it packages agent skills, executes multi-step flows, abstracts LLM providers, and governs agent behaviour through a persistent knowledge base, rule projection, compliance checks, and skill evaluations.
analysis_limits: Full file contents were not available; analysis relies on file paths, symbol names, and directory structure.
Behaviour of individual functions (e.g. FlowRunner.execute, TransitionRegistry internals) is inferred from names and neighbouring components.
No inspection of prompt text inside skill/subagent markdown files; role boundaries inferred from paths.
Concurrency/parallel execution could not be confirmed; assumed sequential unless evidenced.
Runtime traces and evaluation artefacts were not opened.

system_map.overview: CAS is a governance-centric agentic system: a centralised FlowRunner orchestrates multi-step flows, while cognitive work is delegated to packaged skills and a verifier subagent that read from a persistent cas-knowledge base and are constrained by projected rules and compliance checks. LLM access is abstracted behind a client interface with a mock twin for deterministic testing, and agent configuration is merged/synchronised across multiple runtimes (Claude, Gemini, generic AGENTS).

agents.name: Skill Agent
agents.role: Executes a single packaged capability (feature change, module refactor, drawio generation, knowledge-link refactor, archgov review sync, agent-rule audit, HF CLI) as directed by skill markdown instructions

agents.name: Verifier Subagent
agents.role: Independent verification/review of artefacts and changes produced by skills

agents.name: Governance Engine
agents.role: Computes compliance findings/metrics, resolves governance inventory, and executes bounded governance actions via registered transitions

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Central orchestrator that drives multi-step flow execution and passes evolving context between steps

agents.name: LLM Client
agents.role: Provider-agnostic model access (real via LiteLLM, mock for tests) used by agents and steps

orchestration.description: A single FlowRunner drives execution of sequential steps; skills and the verifier subagent are invoked as discrete units, while governance decisions flow through GovernanceActionService -> GovernanceActionEngine -> TransitionRegistry. Rules are projected from cas-knowledge into runtime context files consumed by agents.

tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provider-agnostic access to underlying LLM providers

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLMClient

tools_and_integrations.purpose: Rendering architecture knowledge as a published portal

Per-execution runtime artefacts: rule context, execution profile, traces, evaluations

Flow-step context passed within a FlowRunner execution

patterns.name: Skill-Packaged Agent Capabilities

tool_protocols.notes: Skills invoke shell/tool operations (e.g. drawio, hf-cli) per their markdown instructions

optimisation_targets.notes: Each capability is isolated so its instructions/constraints are portable and auditable

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Capability is scoped per skill; autonomy is limited to the skill's declared task

patterns.summary: Each agent capability is packaged as a self-contained skill directory with its own instructions, allowing discrete, reusable units of agent behaviour.
patterns.intent: Avoid one monolithic agent prompt by partitioning agent behaviour into named, versioned, invokable capabilities.
patterns.context: Appears as a top-level set of cas-* skill directories (feature modification, module refactor, knowledge-link refactor, archgov review sync, drawio generation, agent-rule audit, hf-cli) mirrored into .claude/skills.
forces: Reuse across projects vs. per-project specificity
patterns.solution: Behaviour is defined in per-skill folders rather than a single instruction blob; the runtime orchestrator/CLI selects a skill and the skill's markdown acts as the local contract for that capability.
implementation_signals: Skill names encode the governed operation (cas-*)

evidence.note: Multiple discrete skill directories define agent capabilities
Same skill set exposed to the Claude runtime

benefits: Bounded, auditable agent behaviour per task
failure_modes: Divergent copies of a skill drift between runtimes
A skill's implicit assumptions are not enforced programmatically

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt the skill-as-folder convention (name, instructions, optional assets) and pair it with a runner that selects skills by name.

patterns.name: Sequential Flow Pipeline with Shared Evolving Context

tool_protocols.notes: Steps invoke tools/LLM calls in defined order

optimisation_targets.notes: Ordered steps make execution deterministic and debuggable

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Explicit step ordering constrains agent autonomy to keep flows reproducible

patterns.summary: A central FlowRunner executes an ordered pipeline of steps, threading a shared context through each step.
patterns.intent: Provide deterministic, inspectable multi-step execution instead of letting a model freely decide the sequence.
patterns.context: FlowRunner is the single orchestration entry point for agent flows in cas_runner.
patterns.solution: Execution is expressed as an explicit sequence of steps managed by FlowRunner; each step receives the current context and returns its output, which is carried forward.
implementation_signals: FlowRunner class as sole flow driver
Steps depend on incoming context rather than re-deriving state

evidence.note: Central orchestrator for multi-step flow execution

failure_modes: A failing step halts the whole flow
Context mutation by an early step corrupts later steps

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse as the default control-flow skeleton; plug steps in and pass an explicit context object rather than relying on global state.

patterns.name: Provider Abstraction with Mock Parity

optimisation_targets.notes: Mock client allows deterministic, free CI runs

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Model access is a swappable seam rather than hard-coded provider calls

patterns.summary: All model access goes through a client abstraction with a real LiteLLM implementation and a mock twin for deterministic testing.
patterns.intent: Decouple agent logic from any single LLM provider and enable offline/deterministic test execution.
patterns.context: The llm package defines LiteLLMClient (production) and MockLLMClient (tests/CI) as interchangeable backends.
patterns.solution: Agent code depends on a client interface; LiteLLM provides multi-provider routing while MockLLMClient provides canned responses for tests and CI.
implementation_signals: Two sibling client implementations in src/cas_runner/llm/
CI workflows run without live model credentials

benefits: Swap models/providers without touching agent logic
costs: Mock can diverge from real model behaviour
Interface must cover all needed capabilities
failure_modes: Tests pass against mock but fail against real model
Provider-specific behaviour leaks into the abstraction

patterns.reuse_notes: Define the client contract once, ship a real adapter and a mock adapter, and inject it rather than importing a provider SDK directly.

patterns.name: Governance Action Transition Registry

tool_protocols.notes: Actions are dispatched through service -> engine

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agent-driven governance is bounded by an explicit transition registry

patterns.summary: Governance actions are executed through a registry of permitted state transitions behind a service boundary.
patterns.intent: Prevent unconstrained agent-initiated governance changes by requiring actions to follow registered transitions.
patterns.context: governance_action_engine.py defines TransitionRegistry and GovernanceActionEngine; governance_action_service.py exposes GovernanceActionService; models.py defines GovernanceAction and ResolutionResult.
forces: Autonomy of governance agents vs. safety of allowed transitions
patterns.solution: A registry enumerates legal transitions; the engine validates and executes an action; the service provides the boundary used by callers.

evidence.note: Registry of legal transitions plus executor
Service boundary for invoking governance actions

costs: Registry must be maintained as governance evolves
failure_modes: Incomplete registry blocks legitimate actions
Model drift between registry and real process

patterns.reuse_notes: Encode permitted agent-initiated state changes as an explicit registry; wrap execution in a service so callers cannot bypass validation.

patterns.name: Agentic Configuration Merger

tool_protocols.notes: Config files are the interface to external agent runtimes

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures governance rules survive across runtimes

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agent runtimes receive a managed governance block rather than ad-hoc instructions

patterns.summary: A merger injects a managed governance block into agent runtime configuration files so policies propagate consistently.
patterns.intent: Keep agent runtime configs (CLAUDE.md, settings, etc.) aligned with CAS governance without requiring manual edits.
patterns.context: AgenticMerger plus bootstrap helpers merge_cas_governance_block and merge_claude_settings perform idempotent merges during bootstrap.
patterns.solution: A delimited governance block is merged into target config files, and settings are merged programmatically so repeated runs converge.

evidence.note: Merges governance content into agent configs

costs: Merge logic must handle user edits
failure_modes: Malformed merge corrupts config
User edits outside the block are lost

patterns.reuse_notes: Use an explicit, delimited managed block; merge into rather than overwrite the whole file, and make repeated application idempotent.

patterns.name: Compliance Guardrail Engine

optimisation_targets.notes: Findings and metrics gate agent-produced artefacts

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agent outputs are checked against explicit compliance rules

patterns.summary: A dedicated compliance engine evaluates artefacts against rules and emits typed findings and metrics.
patterns.intent: Provide an automated, typed safety net that constrains and scores agent behaviour against governance rules.
patterns.context: ComplianceEngine produces ComplianceFinding/ComplianceMetrics consumed by the dashboard and governance actions.
patterns.solution: The engine inspects inputs via typed models and produces findings + metrics, which feed health and action decisions.

costs: False positives can block valid work
failure_modes: Stale rules miss new failure modes
Findings without remediation guidance cause friction

patterns.reuse_notes: Model findings and metrics as first-class types so they can feed dashboards, gates, and downstream governance actions.

patterns.name: Assertion-Based Skill Evaluation Suites

tool_protocols.notes: Evals are run in CI against skill behaviour

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Skills keep autonomy but are validated against declared assertions

patterns.summary: Skills ship with declarative eval cases and assertion suites that are executed in CI to catch behavioural regressions.
patterns.intent: Make agent behaviour testable and regression-safe rather than relying on ad-hoc manual review.
patterns.context: skills/models.py defines EvalStatus, SkillAssertions, SkillEvalCase, SkillEvalSuite, SkillEvalResult, SkillEvalReport; cas-skill-evals.yml runs these suites.
patterns.solution: Each skill evaluation is expressed as a suite of cases with assertions; results are aggregated into a report consumed by CI.

failure_modes: Evals pass while real output degrades (overfitting to assertions)
Non-deterministic LLM output causes flaky suites

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt typed eval suites with assertion lists plus an aggregating report; run them in CI and keep assertions behaviour-focused.

patterns.name: Verifier Subagent Delegation

tool_protocols.notes: Delegation is expressed as a subagent specification

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: A dedicated verifier agent adds independent judgement without granting it execution authority

patterns.summary: A dedicated verifier subagent is defined separately from producer skills so verification is an independent, delegated role.
patterns.intent: Separate the agent that produces changes from the agent that verifies them, reducing self-confirmation bias.
patterns.context: Verifier is declared in both the generic agent layer (.agents/subagents) and the Claude runtime (.claude/agents).
forces: Independence of review vs. added latency/cost
patterns.solution: A distinct verifier subagent specification is registered in the agent layer; producer skills and the verifier are separate roles coordinated by the orchestrating runtime.
implementation_signals: verifier.md as a dedicated subagent definition

evidence.note: Verifier role definition in generic agent layer
Verifier registered for the Claude runtime

benefits: Clear role boundary between produce and verify
costs: Two specs to keep in sync
failure_modes: Verifier inherits producer assumptions
Specs drift between runtimes

patterns.reuse_notes: Define verification as a separate agent role with its own instructions rather than an inline check; keep the spec mirrored via symlinks or generated files.

patterns.name: Knowledge Base as Shared Blackboard

tool_protocols.notes: Agents read/write knowledge artefacts as files

optimisation_targets.notes: Shared, durable memory improves consistency across agent runs

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents share a durable knowledge store instead of per-run scratchpads

patterns.summary: A versioned cas-knowledge repository acts as a shared blackboard of patterns, decisions, governance, and project context that agents read and write.
patterns.intent: Give agents durable, shared context so decisions and learnings persist and are reused across runs and projects.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge splits global (decisions, governance, maps, models, narratives, patterns, rules, signals), projects, runtime, and templates.
forces: Durable shared memory vs. context bloat
patterns.solution: Knowledge is organised by concern and scope, reinforced by templates (pattern, decision, experiment, signal), and consumed by agents during execution.
implementation_signals: Runtime folder for traces/evaluations alongside persistent knowledge

evidence.note: Global knowledge areas for patterns, decisions, rules, signals

costs: Risk of stale or conflicting knowledge
failure_modes: Agents write inconsistent artefacts without templates
Knowledge grows without indexing, degrading retrieval

patterns.reuse_notes: Partition memory by scope (global/project/runtime), enforce artefact templates, and treat the store as append-mostly to preserve auditability.

patterns.name: Steering Rule Projection into Runtime Context

tool_protocols.notes: Projected files are the agent input contract

optimisation_targets.notes: Constraints are materialised before execution rather than discovered at runtime

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents receive a pre-resolved rule set, limiting on-the-fly interpretation

patterns.summary: Governance steering rules are projected from the knowledge base into concrete runtime context files consumed by agents.
patterns.intent: Turn curated governance steering into an explicit, machine-readable runtime contract instead of relying on implicit agent memory.
patterns.context: CI workflows build the steering projection and sync managed steering, producing rule-context.json and execution-profile.yaml in cas-knowledge/runtime.
patterns.solution: A projection build step derives runtime rule context from governance sources; agents and workflows consume the projected artefacts.

evidence.note: Projected execution profile for agent runs

failure_modes: Projection out of date relative to governance sources
Agents ignore projected context in favour of stale instructions

patterns.reuse_notes: Materialise policy into explicit runtime files generated from a single source of truth, and rebuild them automatically in CI.

patterns.name: Evidence-Derived Architecture Documentation

tool_protocols.notes: Agents produce docs via skills such as drawio-generator

optimisation_targets.notes: Documentation is regenerated/validated from evidence to resist drift

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agent generates docs, but evidence and templates constrain output

patterns.summary: Architecture documents and diagrams are produced by agent skills from repository evidence using templates, and validated by CI.
patterns.intent: Prevent documentation drift by deriving artefacts from evidence rather than unconstrained generation.
patterns.context: Skills like cas-drawio-generator and cas-refactor-knowledge-links produce/repair documentation; templates fix structure; continuous-architecture workflows validate.
patterns.solution: A template constrains artefact shape, a skill performs the work, and CI validates results against the repository state.
implementation_signals: Richer template set (architecture intent, evolution map, diagram)

costs: Generation quality depends on evidence quality
failure_modes: Generated docs overstate what code supports
Stale evidence yields outdated diagrams

patterns.reuse_notes: Pair a fixed artefact template with a generation skill and a CI validation step to keep agent-written docs honest.

patterns.name: Idempotent Workspace Bootstrap

tool_protocols.notes: Filesystem links/copies wire agent configs into a workspace

optimisation_targets.notes: One command re-establishes a consistent agent workspace

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Workspace setup is deterministic and repeatable

patterns.summary: A bootstrap routine initialises a workspace by merging governance config, linking skills, and emitting an onboarding checklist, converging on repeat runs.
patterns.intent: Make agent workspace setup repeatable and consistent across machines and projects.
patterns.context: bootstrap.py exposes bootstrap, init_workspace, render_onboarding_checklist and _create_symlink_or_copy; cli.py drives it.
patterns.solution: Bootstrap merges managed config, creates symlinks (falling back to copies) for skill directories, and prints a checklist, so reruns converge to the same state.

evidence.note: Workspace initialisation with merge and linking

failure_modes: Copy fallback leads to stale duplicated skills
Partial failure leaves a half-initialised workspace

patterns.reuse_notes: Make setup convergent: merge managed blocks, prefer links with a copy fallback, and always emit a human-readable checklist.

patterns.name: Multi-Runtime Agent Parity

tool_protocols.notes: Per-runtime config adapted for Claude, Gemini, generic agents

optimisation_targets.notes: Same governance applies regardless of runtime

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Runtimes share a common governance baseline

patterns.summary: The same agent guidance and governance is expressed across multiple runtime entry points (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md) and their config directories.
patterns.intent: Keep agent behaviour portable across different agent runtimes without re-authoring policy per runtime.
patterns.context: Top-level AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md plus mirrored .agents/.claude directories and settings.json encode the shared baseline.
patterns.solution: A canonical agent guidance layer is mirrored into runtime-specific entry points, with bootstrap merging the managed governance block into each.

evidence.note: Claude-specific projection of the same guidance

costs: Multiple artefacts to keep in sync
failure_modes: One runtime's file drifts from canonical guidance
Runtime quirks surface only in one projection

patterns.reuse_notes: Maintain one canonical guidance source and generate/mirror per-runtime projections as part of bootstrap.

patterns.name: Derived Governance Health Signal

optimisation_targets.notes: Health summarises governance state for human oversight

patterns.summary: A deterministic health model aggregates governance inventory, throughput, and risk metrics into a status with explanatory reasons.
patterns.intent: Give humans a compact, explainable signal of agent-system health without reading raw governance data.
patterns.context: health_model.py defines HealthStatus, calculate_health, get_health_reasons; governance/models.py supplies TraceableMetric, GovernanceInventory, GovernanceHealth, GovernanceThroughput, GovernanceRisks.
patterns.solution: Metrics are typed and traceable; a pure function computes status and a companion returns human-readable reasons.

costs: Coarse view can mask local issues
failure_modes: Opaque thresholds hide meaningful degradation
Stale inputs produce confidently wrong health

patterns.reuse_notes: Separate metric computation from status derivation, and always pair a status with reason strings for human oversight.

patterns.name: Human-Gated Knowledge Promotion

tool_protocols.notes: Promotion is a documented decision artefact

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents agents from silently elevating unvalidated knowledge

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents propose knowledge; promotion requires explicit decision artefacts

patterns.summary: Knowledge moves from heuristic/experiment to pattern/decision through explicit promotion artefacts, keeping humans in the loop.
patterns.intent: Stop unvalidated agent output from becoming authoritative knowledge by requiring a recorded promotion decision.
patterns.context: Templates for promotion_decision, heuristic-to-pattern, experiment, architecture_decision_record and vision define the lifecycle artefacts agents must produce.
forces: Velocity of learning vs. trust in knowledge
patterns.solution: Distinct artefact types (experiment, learning, heuristic, pattern, decision) with templates; promotion is expressed as its own decision record rather than an implicit edit.

evidence.note: Template for elevating heuristics to patterns

failure_modes: Agents skip promotion and write directly to authoritative areas
Templates filled pro forma without real evidence

patterns.reuse_notes: Model knowledge maturity as distinct artefact types with a dedicated promotion record; never let generation and promotion share one step.

anti_patterns.name: Symlink-or-Copy Config Drift
symptoms: Same skill exists as real directories under both .agents/skills and .claude/skills
Bootstrap falls back to copying when symlinking fails
Runtimes may read different versions of the same skill

where_observed.note: Falls back to copy when symlinks are unavailable

impact: Stale instructions executed by one agent runtime
suggested_remediation: Treat one location as canonical and generate the other
Emit a warning/checksum when falling back to copy
Add a CI check that mirrors are identical or link-backed

anti_patterns.name: Fragmented Governance CI Workflows
symptoms: Six cas-* workflows (continuous-architecture, build-steering-projection, managed-steering-sync, build-validation, portal-publish, skill-evals) with overlapping triggers
A dedicated spec exists to simplify CI/CD workflows (specs/090-simplify-cicd-workflows)
Validation logic lives in a standalone script (validate_workflows.py)

where_observed.note: A validator plus dedicated spec indicates recognised workflow sprawl

impact: Unclear which workflow is authoritative for a given governance check
Duplicated agent/governance invocations increase cost and latency
suggested_remediation: Consolidate into a single orchestrated pipeline with reusable jobs
Use composite actions (already partially adopted per setup-cas) to remove duplication
Retire superseded workflows explicitly and validate against the retirement list

anti_patterns.name: Implicit Merge Overwrite of Agent Config
symptoms: Governance and settings merging happens during bootstrap without visible per-file diff/confirmation
Manual edits outside the managed block may be lost or silently reordered

where_observed.note: Merge helpers run as part of bootstrap

impact: User or team customisations silently reverted
Governance drift between what operators wrote and what runs
Hard to audit what the merge changed
suggested_remediation: Restrict merging to an explicit delimited block and leave surrounding content untouched
Surface a dry-run/diff of merge changes
Record merge provenance in the knowledge base

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Agent behaviour is constrained by skill markdown directories, a managed governance block merged into runtime configs, and templates that fix artefact shape.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Contracts are file-based and human-readable; enforcement depends on runtime compliance plus CI validation rather than a typed prompt schema.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Skill eval suites with assertions plus a compliance engine and derived health model provide layered evaluation of agent output.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Evaluation is split across agent-quality (skill evals), rule-compliance (compliance engine), and system-health (dashboard) axes.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Governance actions are bounded by a transition registry; rule context is projected before runtime; a verifier subagent provides independent review.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Safety relies on explicit allow-lists and precomputed constraints rather than model self-restraint.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: A MockLLMClient enables CI runs without live model calls; multi-runtime configs risk duplicate invocations.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: No explicit token/cost budgeting was observed; cost control is indirect via test doubles and workflow consolidation work.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Runtime traces and evaluations are stored under cas-knowledge/runtime; governance metrics are typed and traceable; health exposes reasons.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Observability is file-based and agent-readable, enabling self-inspection but requiring curation to remain useful.

open_questions.question: How does FlowRunner actually pass state between steps?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether the sequential pipeline pattern is a true shared-context contract or just sequential invocation.
open_questions.evidence_gap: src/cas_runner/runner.py#FlowRunner body was not available; step base contract was not listed in key files.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Inspect src/cas_runner/runner.py and the steps package for context typing, mutation, and error propagation.

open_questions.question: Is there any parallel/fan-out execution in flows or workflows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Concurrency changes cost, latency, and state-safety assumptions for agents.
open_questions.evidence_gap: No concurrency primitives appear in the symbol index; GitHub workflows may run jobs in parallel but this was not inspected.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Search for async/asyncio/gather/thread pools in src/cas_runner and job dependency graphs in .github/workflows/cas-*.yml.

open_questions.question: Do the .claude/skills directories symlink to .agents/skills or are they independent copies?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Drift risk between runtimes depends on whether bootstrap links or copies.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Directory listings cannot distinguish symlinks from real directories.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Check inode/link status of .claude/skills/* and re-run bootstrap to observe _create_symlink_or_copy behaviour.

open_questions.question: What exactly does the verifier subagent verify and with what authority?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Independence of verification is central to the trust model of agent-produced changes.
open_questions.evidence_gap: verifier.md content was not readable in this analysis.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Read .agents/subagents/verifier.md and .claude/agents/verifier.md and compare their instructions.

open_questions.question: Are governance transitions enforced at runtime or only documented?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The TransitionRegistry only constrains behaviour if every mutation path goes through GovernanceActionService.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Call sites of GovernanceActionService were not visible.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Grep for GovernanceActionService usage and confirm no direct mutation of governance state bypasses it.
